violations.title: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY missing
violations.message: Table public.expense_claims has RLS enabled but not FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. The table owner role still bypasses RLS, which often masks broken policies in development and CI. Run `ALTER TABLE public.expense_claims FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;`.

violations.title: All policies on table are permissive
violations.message: Every policy on public.expense_claims is permissive. Permissive policies combine with OR — adding one RESTRICTIVE policy gives a floor (e.g. tenant scoping) that no OR branch can bypass, for the roles in its own TO list. Use TO PUBLIC to bind every role: measured, a restrictive TO authenticated left authenticated at 1 row and another role at 3.

violations.title: Auth function called per-row in policy USING/WITH CHECK
violations.message: Policy 'claimant reads own' on public.expense_claims calls an auth function in USING without wrapping it in a subquery. Postgres re-evaluates the call per row. Wrap as e.g. (SELECT auth.uid()) so the planner caches the result for the whole statement.

violations.title: Auth function called per-row in policy USING/WITH CHECK
violations.message: Policy 'claimant files own' on public.expense_claims calls an auth function in WITH CHECK without wrapping it in a subquery. Postgres re-evaluates the call per row. Wrap as e.g. (SELECT auth.uid()) so the planner caches the result for the whole statement.
